newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks fall for third day.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks fall for third day.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended down for the third consecutive day Friday as foreign funds and local investors continued profit taking after heady New Year rises.
Bogota's IBB index fell 1.84 percent to 1,014.33 amid a 3.5 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED index dropped back 0.64 percent at 16,301.8 amid a 2.3 billion peso volume.
"In general the markets were a little slow. There was quite a lot of offer and the volumes that came on to the market tend to suggest it was the foreign funds selling," one Bogota broker said.
The biggest decliner on the Bogota exchange was cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, down 4.46 percent to 5,350. Banco de Colombia lost 3.21 percent, closing down at 452.
"The falls in Caribe and Banco de Colombia are due to small investors cashing in their profits. The price correction seems likely to continue," another Bogota broker said.

The biggest volumes centered around brewing giant Bavaria. It fell 1.43 percent to 6,100 amid a 2.4 billion peso volume in Bogota. Overall, Colombia's two main stock price indices have risen more than 22 percent in the year to date, even taking into account the latest falls.

Some analysts predict prices to fall back between five percent and 10 percent before climbing again at the start of the second quarter as companies post year-end results and as first quarter results start filtering through.

The biggest faller on the Medellin exchange was steel manufacturer Acerias Paz del Rio, which lost 14.29 percent to close at 1.80. Finance company Corfinsura fell four percent to end at 2,400 while Cementos Caribe dropped 3.57 percent to 5,400.
